Write \(\mathbf 1=\mathbf 1_K\), let \(\mathbf e_k\) be the \(k\)-th coordinate column, and put
\[
 D=\operatorname{diag}(h),\qquad Q=I_K-D,\qquad
 A=\mathbf e_i(\mathbf e_j-\mathbf e_i)^{\top},\qquad
 S(t)=I_K+tA.                                                   \tag{1}
\]
The equality of the emission profiles of states \(i\) and \(j\) gives
\[
 A\mathbf 1=0,\qquad AB_a=B_aA\quad(a\in\mathcal Y).         \tag{2}
\]
Indeed, the first identity follows from \((\mathbf e_j-\mathbf e_i)^{\top}\mathbf 1=0\), and the second follows because the \(i\)-th and \(j\)-th diagonal entries of every \(B_a\) coincide. The matrix \(S(t)\) agrees with \(I_K\) outside row \(i\), while row \(i\) has entries \(1-t\) in column \(i\) and \(t\) in column \(j\). Expansion along all unchanged rows therefore gives
\[
 \det S(t)=1-t.                                                 \tag{3}
\]
Thus \(S(t)\) is invertible for all \(t\) in a neighborhood of zero, and (2) yields \(S(t)\mathbf 1=\mathbf 1\) and \(S(t)B_a=B_aS(t)\).

For such \(t\), define
\[
 \alpha(t)=\alpha S(t),\qquad h(t)=S(t)^{-1}h,\qquad
 K_0(t)=S(t)^{-1}K_0S(t),                                      \tag{4}
\]
\[
 D(t)=\operatorname{diag}\{h(t)\},\qquad
 P(t)=\{I_K-D(t)\}^{-1}K_0(t),                                \tag{5}
\]
and leave all emission matrices \(B_a\) fixed. At \(t=0\), the entries of \(\alpha\) and \(P\), all hazards and survivals, and all emission probabilities are strictly positive by the hypotheses of the theorem. These are finitely many strict inequalities. The maps in (3)--(5) are continuous wherever \(S(t)\) and \(I_K-D(t)\) are invertible. Hence, after shrinking the neighborhood of zero, \(\alpha(t)\), \(P(t)\), \(h(t)\), and the survivals remain strictly positive. Because the emissions do not move, the entire emission-equality partition, and not merely the equality of the \(i\)-th and \(j\)-th profiles, is fixed along the path.

The matrices in (4)--(5) obey the probability normalizations. Since \(K_0=QP\), stochasticity of \(P\) implies
\[
 K_0\mathbf 1=Q\mathbf 1=\mathbf 1-h.                         \tag{6}
\]
Using \(S(t)\mathbf 1=\mathbf 1\) in (4) and then (6),
\[
 K_0(t)\mathbf 1
 =S(t)^{-1}K_0\mathbf 1
 =S(t)^{-1}(\mathbf 1-h)
 =\mathbf 1-h(t).                                               \tag{7}
\]
Equations (5) and (7) therefore give \(P(t)\mathbf 1=\mathbf 1\). Likewise,
\[
 \alpha(t)\mathbf 1=\alpha S(t)\mathbf 1=\alpha\mathbf 1=1. \tag{8}
\]
Thus each sufficiently small perturbation is a legal homogeneous stopped-HMM realization. Conditional adoption coins can be generated with probabilities \(h(t)\) independently of current and future untreated innovations given the current hidden state; hence the current-state hazard and future-innovation independence conditions remain satisfied. Moreover,
\[
 \det K_0(t)=\det\{S(t)^{-1}K_0S(t)\}=\det K_0\ne0,          \tag{9}
\]
and the predictive rank is preserved by the observable-law equalities proved next. Thus the path remains in the fixed-emission-partition realization stratum over \(\mathcal M^{\mathrm{stop}}_{K,T}\).

For \(a\in\mathcal Y\), let \(M_a(t)=B_aK_0(t)\). Commutation in (2) and (4) imply
\[
 M_a(t)=B_aS(t)^{-1}K_0S(t)=S(t)^{-1}M_aS(t).                 \tag{10}
\]
Consequently, for every word \(w=(a_1,\ldots,a_\ell)\), including the empty word,
\[
 M_w(t)=S(t)^{-1}M_wS(t).                                     \tag{11}
\]
The risk- and adoption-terminal stopped series therefore satisfy
\[
 \alpha(t)M_w(t)\mathbf 1
 =\alpha M_w\mathbf 1,\qquad
 \alpha(t)M_w(t)h(t)=\alpha M_wh.                             \tag{12}
\]
By the definition of the stopped series, (12) proves equality of every pre-adoption stopped-word probability, for every available word length. For every member of the path, take the conditional distribution of post-adoption realized outcomes given the adoption time and observed stopped history to equal that under the original realization. This construction can be implemented by common post-adoption innovation kernels, preserves consistency and no anticipation, and, together with (12), gives exactly the same complete observed-panel law \(P_W\) for all sufficiently small \(t\).

The path is a genuine continuum. Differentiating \(h(t)=S(t)^{-1}h\) at zero gives
\[
 \dot h(0)=-Ah=-(h_j-h_i)\mathbf e_i\ne0.                    \tag{13}
\]
The derivative of the \(i\)-th coordinate is nonzero at zero, so continuity of that derivative permits the interval to be shrunk until \(h_i(t)\) is strictly monotone. The realization path is then injective on that interval. Every permutation-equivalence class has cardinality at most \(K!\); hence the quotient of this injective interval by latent permutations is still uncountable and contains a continuum of non-permutation representatives. Since the path converges to the original realization as \(t\to0\), every relatively open neighborhood in the fixed-partition stratum contains such a continuum.

It remains to calculate the causal continuation. Equality of the two emission profiles also gives \(e_i=e_j\), and therefore
\[
 Ae=0,\qquad S(t)e=e,\qquad S(t)^{-1}e=e.                    \tag{14}
\]
The cohort mass is constant along the path:
\[
 p_g(t)=\alpha(t)K_0(t)^gh(t)
 =\alpha K_0^gh=p_g.                                          \tag{15}
\]
To express the alternative causal numerator in the original coordinates, set
\[
 J(t)=S(t)D(t)S(t)^{-1},\qquad
 P_J(t)=\{I_K-J(t)\}^{-1}K_0.                                 \tag{16}
\]
Equations (4), (5), (14), and (16) yield
\[
 \alpha(t)K_0(t)^gD(t)P(t)e
 =\alpha K_0^gJ(t)P_J(t)e.                                    \tag{17}
\]
The current-state hazard condition and future-innovation independence give, under the realization at \(t\),
\[
 \mathbb E_t\!\left[\nu\{Y_{g+1}(\infty)\}\mathbf 1\{G=g\}\right]
 =\alpha(t)K_0(t)^gD(t)P(t)e.                                  \tag{18}
\]
Here \(K_0(t)^g\) propagates through the \(g\) survived periods, \(D(t)\) selects adoption from the current hidden state, \(P(t)\) propagates the untreated state one period, and \(e\) integrates the next untreated emission. Thus (15), (17), and (18), with division justified by \(p_g>0\), give
\[
 \mu^0_{g,1}(t)=\frac{\alpha K_0^gJ(t)P_J(t)e}{p_g}.          \tag{19}
\]

We now differentiate this quotient. From \(S'(0)=A\), \((S^{-1})'(0)=-A\), and (13),
\[
\begin{aligned}
 \dot J(0)
 &=AD-\operatorname{diag}(Ah)-DA\\
 &=[A,D]-\operatorname{diag}(Ah)\\
 &=(h_j-h_i)\mathbf e_i(\mathbf e_j-\mathbf e_i)^{\top}.
                                                                    \tag{20}
\end{aligned}
\]
In particular, \(\dot J(0)\mathbf 1=0\). The defining identity \(\{I_K-J(t)\}P_J(t)=K_0\) has derivative \(-\dot J(0)P+(I_K-D)\dot P_J(0)=0\). Since every survival is positive, \(I_K-D\) is invertible, and hence
\[
 \dot P_J(0)=(I_K-D)^{-1}\dot J(0)(I_K-D)^{-1}K_0
 =(I_K-D)^{-1}\dot J(0)P.                                    \tag{21}
\]
Since \(I_K+D(I_K-D)^{-1}=(I_K-D)^{-1}\), equations (19)--(21) imply
\[
\begin{aligned}
 \left.\frac{d}{dt}\mu^0_{g,1}(t)\right|_{t=0}
 &=\frac{\alpha K_0^g\{\dot J(0)Pe+D(I_K-D)^{-1}\dot J(0)Pe\}}{p_g}\\
 &=\frac{\alpha K_0^g(I_K-D)^{-1}\dot J(0)Pe}{p_g}\\
 &=\frac{(\alpha K_0^g)_i(h_j-h_i)\{(Pe)_j-(Pe)_i\}}
 {(1-h_i)p_g}.                                                  \tag{22}
\end{aligned}
\]
Every denominator in (22) is positive. Specifically, the interior-hazard condition gives \(1-h_i>0\); strict positivity of \(P\) and of \(1-h\) makes \(K_0=QP\) entrywise positive; strict positivity of \(\alpha\) then makes every coordinate of \(\alpha K_0^g\) positive; and multiplication by the positive hazard column gives \(p_g=\alpha K_0^gh>0\). The two contrasts in the hypotheses are nonzero, so (22) is nonzero for every supported \(g\). There are only finitely many such cohort indices. Continuity of their derivatives and a minimum over finitely many neighborhoods give one interval on which each derivative keeps its nonzero sign. Every corresponding function \(\mu^0_{g,1}(t)\) is therefore strictly monotone on that interval, so distinct path points give different values for every supported cohort. The observed treated-outcome law was held fixed, so \(\mu^1_{g,1}\) is constant and \(\tau_{g,1}=\mu^1_{g,1}-\mu^0_{g,1}\) changes with the opposite sign. This proves every assertion of the narrowed theorem.

\[
 S(a,b)=\begin{pmatrix}a&1-a\\ b&1-b\end{pmatrix},\qquad a\ne b,

and let \(h_{12}=(h_1,h_2)^{\top}\). If \(h_1\ne h_2\), the rational map

proposed_definition_changes.proposed:
Fix \(K=3\), \(T=5\), \((g,r)=(0,1)\), the binary alphabet ordered as \(0<1\), the chart \(\mathcal U=(\epsilon,0,1)\), and \(\mathcal V=((\epsilon,R),(\epsilon,A),(0,A))\). Under the baseline-symbol convention in \(\mathcal D_{K-1}\), fix \(\mathcal D_2=(I_3,\bar B_1,\bar B_1^2)\), \(\mathcal F=(I_3,\bar B_1)\), and \(d=2\). For sufficiently small parameters \(\eta>0\) and \(\zeta>0\), set
\[
 h^{(0)}(\eta)=\left(\frac3{20}-\eta,\frac3{20}+\eta,\frac9{20}\right)^{\top},
 \qquad
 B_1^{\star}(\zeta)=\operatorname{diag}\left(\frac15,\frac15+\zeta,\frac45\right),
 \qquad B_0^{\star}(\zeta)=I_3-B_1^{\star}(\zeta),
\]
and, using the fixed \(\alpha_{\star}\), \(P_{\star}\), and \(S_{\star}\), set
\[
 \alpha^{(1)}=\alpha_{\star}S_{\star},\qquad
 h^{(1)}(\eta)=S_{\star}^{-1}h^{(0)}(\eta),
\]
\[
 K_0^{(1)}(\eta)=S_{\star}^{-1}
 \{I_3-\operatorname{diag}(h^{(0)}(\eta))\}P_{\star}S_{\star},
 \qquad
 P^{(1)}(\eta)=\{I_3-\operatorname{diag}(h^{(1)}(\eta))\}^{-1}K_0^{(1)}(\eta).
\]
Let \(P_W^{(0)}(\eta,\zeta)\) be the six-date stopped-panel law induced by \((\alpha_{\star},P_{\star},h^{(0)}(\eta),B_0^{\star}(\zeta),B_1^{\star}(\zeta))\), and let \(P_W^{(1)}(\eta,\zeta)\) be the law induced by \((\alpha^{(1)},P^{(1)}(\eta),h^{(1)}(\eta),B_0^{\star}(\zeta),B_1^{\star}(\zeta))\), with the same deterministic treated-outcome law in both cases. Define
\[
 \mathfrak C(\eta,\zeta)=
 \bigl(P_W^{(0)}(\eta,\zeta),P_W^{(1)}(\eta,\zeta)\bigr),
\]
and evaluate its causal separation only through \(\mu^0_{0,1}\) and \(\tau_{0,1}\). The sequences \(\mathfrak C(\eta_N,\zeta_N)\), including \(\eta_N=N^{-1/4}\), \(\zeta_N=N^{-1}\), are instances of this two-parameter family rather than part of its definition.
proposed_definition_changes.reason: The collision construction is intrinsically a two-parameter positive family. Hard-wiring \(\eta_N=N^{-1/4}\) and \(\zeta_N=N^{-1}\) into its definition hides the fixed-\(\eta\) subfamily that yields nonuniform-consistency impossibility and incorrectly turns one useful sequence into the construction itself.

proposed_definition_changes.proposed:
Restrict to \(\mathcal S^{+}_{2+1}\) and fix \((g,r)=(0,1)\). Form, from rational fixed-chart stopped-law coordinates, the similarity-invariant projector onto the emission-distinct state and its complementary two-state alias block. On the alias block retain the full row-stochastic centralizer
\[
 S(a,b)=\begin{pmatrix}a&1-a\\ b&1-b\end{pmatrix},\qquad a\ne b,
\]
embedded by the identity on the emission-distinct state. Express the transformed initial row, the transformed hazard
\[
 S(a,b)\operatorname{diag}\{S(a,b)^{-1}h_{12}\}S(a,b)^{-1},
\]
where \(h_{12}=(h_1,h_2)^{\top}\), the killed dynamics, and the de-killed transition as bivariate rational functions of \((a,b)\). Define the positive legal region by all normalization, nonvanishing-denominator, and strict positivity inequalities required by \(\mathcal L_{\mathrm{legal}}\). Clear only denominators certified nonzero on each positive legal component. Test constancy of every coordinate of \(\pi^0_{0,1}\) by bivariate rational numerator identities on that component. Separate the HDK branch from every forecast-degenerate branch on which HDK fails but the target is constant. A reduction to univariate sign problems is permitted only after a proved elimination or parameterization; connectedness is not imported from an ordinary aliased-HMM model. Use subresultant chains and Sturm--Habicht sign determination when such a reduction has been proved, record every polynomial or rational invariant and its degree, and enumerate every positive legal-fiber component. The computation exploits the fixed one-block dimension rather than invoking generic cylindrical algebraic decomposition.
proposed_definition_changes.reason: The full row-stochastic centralizer of a two-state alias block has two parameters \(a,b\) with \(a\ne b\). Unequal hazards give a nonzero two-dimensional Jacobian minor, and strict legality inequalities do not collapse the local dimension. A predeclared univariate reduction therefore assumes geometry that has not been proved; constancy must first be tested as a bivariate rational problem on each positive legal component.

proposed.statement: Fix \(K=3\), \(T=5\), \(\mathcal Y=\{0,1\}\), \((g,r)=(0,1)\), and \(P_W\in\mathcal S^{+}_{2+1}\). The stratification must separate the HDK branch from every forecast-degenerate branch on which HDK fails but the target remains constant, list explicit polynomial or rational invariants and their degrees, and enumerate every positive legal-fiber component. proposed.comparator_claim: The paper studies an ordinary all-length stationary parametric-output HMM with exactly two aliased states under A1 output-family linear independence of order \(n\) and A2 ergodicity with a strictly positive stationary law, and characterizes its non-permutation equivalence.
Theorem 1 identifies ATT from repeated measurements, while Section 3.3 states that evolving hidden shocks create a staggered-selection failure for that construction.
Theorem 1 identifies group-time ATT under conditional parallel trends and the paper establishes simultaneous multiplier-bootstrap inference.

Under an interactive fixed-effects law for untreated outcomes and adoption-group moment and rank conditions, the main identification theorem recovers group-time ATT from observed cohort moments, with joint asymptotic inference developed in Proposition 1 and the multiplier-bootstrap corollary.
Theorem 6 bounds HMM prediction error under observable singular-value separation.
Proposition 1 represents the spectral HMM estimator as an equivalent moment estimator, and Section 3.4 optimizes its moment weighting.

The paper estimates effects of a dynamic treatment on potential latent-state distributions by inverse-probability-weighted hidden-Markov maximum likelihood under observed-confounder treatment assignment assumptions.

The paper combines a bias-adjusted three-step latent Markov measurement model with a parametric g-formula under exchangeability, positivity, consistency, no interference, and latent-Markov restrictions.
The paper identifies staggered-adoption effects by design-based matching on observed histories under its stated identifying conditions and applies the method to six-period Netflix--IPTV data.
The paper develops estimation and inference across weak, semi-strong, and strong identification sequences.

 -\frac{(h_1-h_2)^2}{(a-b)^4}.
\]
Hence unequal hazards give two locally independent hazard-lift directions at every strictly positive legal point; the strict legality inequalities do not collapse the local parameter dimension. Along the explicit alias-preserving direction used in the generic converse, unequal one-step forecasts give
\[
 \left.\frac{d}{dt}\mu^0_{0,1}(t)\right|_{t=0}
 =\frac{\alpha_i(h_j-h_i)\{(Pe)_j-(Pe)_i\}}{(1-h_i)p_0}\ne0,
\]
so the target fiber is not a singleton at every unequal-hazard, unequal-forecast point covered by that direction. What remains is the forecast-degenerate HDK-failure locus: its bivariate rational target numerators and positive legal-region components have not been explicitly enumerated, and no univariate reduction or fixed-coefficient-bit-complexity bound has yet been proved.

prose_updates.tldr: State-dependent adoption generally defeats observed-history parallel-trends comparisons because missing future untreated outcomes are selected by latent state. A finite stopped-panel law nevertheless identifies every adopter cohort's untreated path law when adoption hazards are constant within current-emission alias classes. Predictive rank gives chart-independent minimal coordinates, while computation and inference use a preregistered Hankel chart. On a fixed emission-partition stratum, unequal within-alias hazards and one-step forecasts generate a continuum of same-observed-law realizations with different ATT. The exact positive witness has ATT gap \(2/185\). More strongly, the two-parameter family \(\mathfrak C(\eta,\zeta)\) has one-panel divergence \(O(\zeta^2)\) while its target gap is first order in \(\eta\); fixed positive \(\eta\) and \(N\zeta_N^2\to0\) rule out uniform consistency and uniformly honest shrinking bands over the full unseparated neighborhood. The \(N^{-1/4}\) statement is a local corollary. The exceptional binary three-state legal-lift frontier is genuinely bivariate and remains open, as does the Kim--Lee empirical certificate.

project_justification.gap: Staggered-DiD and interactive-fixed-effects methods use observed histories or adoption-cohort moments, while causal latent-Markov procedures impose their own recovery and ignorability structures. Weiss and Nadler are an algebraic ancestor, not a containing model: they study an ordinary all-length stationary parametric-output HMM with exactly two aliased states under A1 output-family linear independence of order \(n\) and A2 ergodicity with a positive stationary law. This stopped two-terminal model permits arbitrary \(\alpha\), and its binary \(K=3\) instance cannot satisfy A1 because three binary probability mass functions lie in a two-dimensional function space. Neither class contains the other, so no Weiss--Nadler converse transfers. Existing spectral results also do not select a preregistered stopped-Hankel minor or identify cohort continuation from an adoption terminal.
project_justification.niche: The observable adoption terminal can identify a similarity-invariant hazard operator even when non-permutation latent realizations share the stopped law. The converse is stated only on a fixed emission-partition stopped-HMM stratum. Near the repeated-emission boundary, the independent hazard- and emission-splitting parameters expose both local weak separation and failure of any nontrivial uniform rate without a coupling restriction.
project_justification.fill: The project proves hazard-lift path-law invariance, a fixed-partition generic converse, and an exact \(2/185\) stress test; supplies a total guarded fixed-chart estimator with regular-subset simultaneous inference; and strengthens the collision analysis to the two-parameter family \(\mathfrak C(\eta,\zeta)\), including nonuniform-consistency and nonshrinking-band impossibility over the displayed unseparated neighborhood. It leaves the complete bivariate one-alias-block legal-lift frontier, with explicit invariants and component enumeration, as an open question, and separately leaves the Kim--Lee empirical certificate open.

prose_updates.related_work: Weiss and Nadler study an ordinary all-length stationary parametric-output HMM with exactly two aliased states, A1 output-family linear independence of order \(n\), and A2 ergodic transition with a strictly positive stationary law. Their similarity calculations are an algebraic ancestor of the legal-fiber construction, but their class neither contains nor is contained in this stopped two-terminal class: the latter allows arbitrary \(\alpha\), while three binary emission mass functions cannot meet their A1 linear-independence condition. Their connectedness and converse conclusions therefore are not imported. Allman, Matias, and Rhodes establish generic finite-window identification, while Gassiat, Cleynen, and Robin and Alexandrovich, Holzmann, and Leister use separation conditions that exclude exact repeated emissions. Bartolucci and Farcomeni give a killed-forward latent event-history model without the proposed causal invariant. Pennoni, Paas, and Bartolucci use propensity-weighted hidden-Markov likelihood, and Clouth, Bijlsma, Pauws, and Vermunt use a fitted latent Markov measurement model inside a parametric g-formula. The fixed-partition generic converse diagnoses transporting those workflows while additionally demanding continuation determined by the observed stopped law; their own structural assumptions are not contradicted, and hazard lifting does not identify their latent-state estimands. Callaway and Sant'Anna identify group-time ATT and simultaneous inference under conditional parallel trends. Callaway and Tsyawo use interactive fixed effects and adoption-date moments; their functional has neither a state-dependent stopping mark nor alias-fiber invariance, while hazard lifting does not impose their factor structure. Kim and Lee use observed-history matching in the six-period Netflix--IPTV panel, and Ishimaru uses repeated measurements outside evolving hidden selection. The exact pair and the two-parameter collision family are stress tests, not contradictions of those papers, because their identifying assumptions are not asserted on the displayed laws. Hsu, Kakade, and Zhang provide ordinary-HMM observable operators, but predictive rank guarantees only that some minor is nonsingular. Tran, Kim, and Doshi-Velez provide a moment-estimation template but not the stopped-chart, de-killing, or frame conditions. Andrews and Cheng provide weak-identification precedent; the collision result is scoped to the displayed family and does not contradict any comparator theorem or separated regular domain. These sources are informed-by comparators, not results claimed to be strictly tightened.
prose_updates.technical_internal_limitation: Sampling noise destroys exact commutativity and repeated eigenvalues, so the estimator uses a fixed written-order polynomial dictionary and a least-squares off-model extension. Full stopped-Hankel rank ensures that some \(K\)-minor works, not that the ordered \(H_{\mathcal U,\mathcal V}\) fixed before outcomes does; all Euclidean separation claims use that chart and coefficient normalization. The total estimator applies inverse formulas only behind fixed half-gap gates and otherwise returns preregistered defaults. For the displayed collision family, both members are legal hazard-lift laws for all sufficiently small \(\eta,\zeta>0\), one-panel KL divergence is \(O(\zeta^2)\), and \(\sigma_3(V_D)=\Theta(\zeta)\), with coefficient \(6250/(17\sqrt{1266})\) as \(\eta\to0\). The counterfactual gap is \(63\eta/544+O(\eta^2+\zeta)\). Thus \(N\zeta_N^2\to0\) and \(\zeta_N=o(\eta_N)\) make the product laws merge while preserving either a first-order local gap or, for fixed small \(\eta_0>0\), a nonzero limiting gap. Without a coupling restriction between hazard and emission splitting, the full unseparated neighborhood has no nontrivial uniform rate. The legal-frontier region is bivariate; univariate sign methods require a proved reduction.
prose_updates.honest_scope: The point-identification theorem fixes the hidden order and finite alphabet, uses \(T\ge2K-1\), and assumes homogeneous untreated dynamics, invertible killed dynamics, positive cohort masses, and sequential hazard randomization. It identifies finite untreated cohort path laws, not latent labels, transitions, or initial probabilities. Predictive rank gives a chart-independent minimal realization and guarantees existence of some nonsingular minor; displayed formulas and inference additionally require the preregistered \(H_{\mathcal U,\mathcal V}\). The generic converse concerns future lags and is proved within a fixed emission-partition realization stratum of \(\mathcal M^{\mathrm{stop}}_{K,T}\). The exact \(2/185\) witness and collision family concern only \(K=3\), \(T=5\), \(g=0\), and \(r=1\). The collision impossibility is over the displayed full unseparated hazard-lift neighborhood: it rules out uniform consistency and uniformly honest \(o(1)\)-diameter bands there, while making no claim against comparator methods on their own maintained domains. Fixed-gap compact regular subsets retain pointwise root-\(N\) inference. The open legal-lift classification is restricted to the positive interior binary three-state, six-date, one-alias-block stratum and now requires a complete bivariate component analysis; no connectedness is imported from Weiss--Nadler. The Kim--Lee data are unavailable, so no empirical certificate is claimed. Unknown order, continuous outcomes, approximate homogeneity, sharp tolerance bounds, adaptive chart selection, constrained-model efficiency, and finite-sample remainders remain open.

proofs.proof_tex:
Apply \(\operatorname{prop:two\text{-}parameter\text{-}collision\text{-}modulus}\) to the declared specialization
\[
 \eta_N=N^{-1/4},\qquad \zeta_N=N^{-1}.                       \tag{33}
\]
The legality calculation (1)--(8) of that proposition gives strict positivity of both realizations and \(p_0>0\) for all sufficiently large \(N\). Its similarity identities (9)--(11) give exact equality of all stopped-word probabilities at \(\zeta_N=0\). Its uniform finite-support bound (13) yields
\[
 \operatorname{KL}(P_{W,N}^{(0)},P_{W,N}^{(1)})=O(\zeta_N^2)=O(N^{-2}). \tag{34}
\]
For finite product laws, expanding the product log-density gives
\[
 \operatorname{KL}\!\left((P_{W,N}^{(0)})^{\otimes N},
                            (P_{W,N}^{(1)})^{\otimes N}\right)
 =N\operatorname{KL}(P_{W,N}^{(0)},P_{W,N}^{(1)})=O(N^{-1}). \tag{35}
\]
Because \((\eta_N,\zeta_N)\to(0,0)\), the singular-value limit (20) in that proposition gives
\[
 \sigma_3(V_D)
 =\left(\frac{6250}{17\sqrt{1266}}+o(1)\right)\zeta_N
 =\{10.332710061\ldots+o(1)\}\zeta_N.                       \tag{36}
\]
The exact bivariate mean formula (22), together with \(\zeta_N=\eta_N^4=o(\eta_N)\), gives
\[
 (\mu^0_{0,1})^{(1)}-(\mu^0_{0,1})^{(0)}
 =\left(\frac{63}{544}+o(1)\right)\eta_N.                   \tag{37}
\]
The treated outcome is the same deterministic constant under both laws, so the ATT gap is the negative of (37) and has magnitude of order \(N^{-1/4}\).

The chi-square product calculation (25)--(27) of the stronger proposition applies because \(N\zeta_N^2=N^{-1}\to0\), and hence the product-law total variation tends to zero. Also, by (36) and \(\rho_N=c_{\rho}\sqrt{\log N/N}\) with \(c_{\rho}>0\),
\[
 0<\frac{\sigma_3(V_D)}{\rho_N}
 =O\!\left(\frac{N^{-1}}{\sqrt{\log N/N}}\right)=o(1),      \tag{38}
\]
so the path eventually lies in \(0<\sigma_3(V_D)\le\rho_N\), the sampling-noise component of \(\mathcal Z_{\mathrm{gray},N}\).

Finally, let \(C_N\) be any confidence band with coverage at least \(1-\alpha_0-o(1)\) under both product laws, and denote their two ATT values by \(\vartheta_{0,N}\) and \(\vartheta_{1,N}\). Total-variation merging transfers the second law's coverage event to the first law, and the union bound gives
\[
 \Pr_{(P_{W,N}^{(0)})^{\otimes N}}\{\vartheta_{0,N}\in C_N,\ \vartheta_{1,N}\in C_N\}
 \ge1-2\alpha_0-o(1)>0.                                      \tag{39}
\]
On this event, (37) forces
\[
 \operatorname{diam}(C_N)\ge|\vartheta_{1,N}-\vartheta_{0,N}|
 =\left(\frac{63}{544}+o(1)\right)N^{-1/4}.                 \tag{40}
\]
Thus diameter \(o(N^{-1/4})\) in probability under both laws is incompatible with uniform \(1-\alpha_0\) coverage. Equations (33)--(40) prove every assertion of the target.

added_lemmas.statement:
Fix the two-parameter construction in \(\operatorname{def:collision\text{-}path}\). There is \(\varepsilon>0\) such that, for every \(0<\eta,\zeta<\varepsilon\), both \(P_0^{\eta,\zeta}\) and \(P_1^{\eta,\zeta}\) belong to \(\mathcal M^{\mathrm{HL}}_{3,5}\), have strictly positive parameters and cohort masses, and have three distinct binary emission profiles. Uniformly on this positive rectangle,
\[
 \operatorname{KL}(P_0^{\eta,\zeta},P_1^{\eta,\zeta})=O(\zeta^2),
 \qquad
 \sigma_3\{V_D(P_0^{\eta,\zeta})\}=\Theta(\zeta),
\]
and, as \((\eta,\zeta)\to(0,0)\) through positive values,
\[
 \frac{\sigma_3\{V_D(P_0^{\eta,\zeta})\}}{\zeta}
 \longrightarrow \frac{6250}{17\sqrt{1266}}.
\]
Writing \(\Delta(\eta,\zeta)=(\mu^0_{0,1})^{(1)}-(\mu^0_{0,1})^{(0)}\), one has
\[
 \Delta(\eta,\zeta)
 =-\frac{3\{87500\eta^3\zeta+18000\eta^2\zeta+9000\eta^2+22015\eta\zeta+53550\eta-3468\zeta\}}
 {400(5\eta+12)(25\eta-17)(25\eta+17)}
 =\frac{63}{544}\eta+O(\eta^2+\zeta).
\]
Consequently, for any positive sequences \(a_N,b_N\) satisfying \(Nb_N^2\to0\) and \(b_N=o(a_N)\), the product laws formed from \(\mathfrak C(a_N,b_N)\) merge in total variation. If \(a_N\to0\), their ATT gap is \((63/544+o(1))a_N\); if \(a_N\equiv\eta_0\) for a sufficiently small fixed \(\eta_0>0\), their ATT gap tends to the nonzero number \(\Delta(\eta_0,0)\) in absolute value. Both sequence types lie eventually in the sampling-noise component of \(\mathcal Z_{\mathrm{gray},N}\). Hence no estimator of \(\tau_{0,1}\) is uniformly consistent, and for each fixed \(\alpha_0<1/2\) no uniformly honest \(1-\alpha_0\) confidence band has diameter \(o(1)\) in probability, over any unseparated \(\mathcal M^{\mathrm{HL}}_{3,5}\) neighborhood containing this displayed positive family. In particular, \(\eta_N=N^{-1/4}\), \(\zeta_N=N^{-1}\) gives an ATT gap \((63/544+o(1))N^{-1/4}\), product-law total variation tending to zero, \(\sigma_3(V_D)=(6250/(17\sqrt{1266})+o(1))N^{-1}\), and impossibility of uniformly honest diameter \(o(N^{-1/4})\) over the displayed pair.
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
Write \(S=S_{\star}\), and choose \(\varepsilon>0\) below small enough for every continuity argument that follows. We first verify legality rather than assuming it. Direct multiplication gives
\[
 \alpha^{(1)}=\alpha_{\star}S
 =\left(\frac{31}{100},\frac{39}{100},\frac3{10}\right),
 \qquad
 h^{(1)}(\eta)=S^{-1}h^{(0)}(\eta)
 =\left(\frac3{20}-\frac54\eta,\frac3{20}+\frac54\eta,\frac9{20}\right)^{\!\top}. \tag{1}
\]
At \(\eta=0\), de-killing the second killed transition gives
\[
 P^{(1)}(0)=
 \begin{pmatrix}
 49/80&5/16&3/40\\
 3/16&39/80&13/40\\
 11/100&19/100&7/10
 \end{pmatrix}.                                                \tag{2}
\]
All entries of both rows in (1), all entries in (2), and all entries of \(\alpha_{\star}\) and \(P_{\star}\) are strictly positive. The entries of \(P^{(1)}(\eta)\) are continuous wherever the components of \(1-h^{(1)}(\eta)\) are positive. Thus, after reducing \(\varepsilon\), both initial rows, both transitions, and all hazards and survival probabilities are strictly positive for \(0\le\eta<\varepsilon\). Their finitely many hazard and survival coordinates consequently have a common positive lower bound on the closed rectangle, which supplies the hazard-overlap constant required by the model class. Stochasticity of the transformed transition is an identity, not an additional premise. Since \(S\mathbf 1_3=\mathbf 1_3\),
\[
 K_0^{(1)}(\eta)\mathbf 1_3
 =S^{-1}K_0^{(0)}(\eta)S\mathbf 1_3
 =S^{-1}\{\mathbf 1_3-h^{(0)}(\eta)\}
 =\mathbf 1_3-h^{(1)}(\eta),                                  \tag{3}
\]
and hence \(P^{(1)}(\eta)\mathbf 1_3=\mathbf 1_3\). For \(0<\zeta<\varepsilon\), the three probabilities \(1/5\), \(1/5+\zeta\), and \(4/5\) are distinct and strictly between zero and one; the complementary zero-emission probabilities have the same properties. Therefore all three emission profiles are distinct, so the within-emission-profile hazard condition defining \(\mathcal M^{\mathrm{HL}}_{3,5}\) holds vacuously.

The remaining model-class conditions also hold. The displayed construction is a time-homogeneous hidden Markov law. Sampling adoption at each risk date from the current state before drawing the current and future untreated innovations enforces the current-state hazard and future-innovation-independence conditions; defining the common post-adoption outcome path and setting the observed path equal to its corresponding potential path enforces consistency and no anticipation. The horizon equality is
\[
 T=5=2\cdot3-1=2K-1.                                         \tag{4}
\]
For killed invertibility, direct evaluation gives \(\det(P_{\star})=7/50\), whence
\[
 \det K_0^{(0)}(\eta)
 =\prod_{s=1}^3\{1-h_s^{(0)}(\eta)\}\det(P_{\star})\ne0,
 \qquad
 \det K_0^{(1)}(\eta)=\det K_0^{(0)}(\eta)\ne0.              \tag{5}
\]
Every cohort mass through date five is positive because, for \(j=0,1\),
\[
 p_g^{(j)}=\alpha^{(j)}\{K_0^{(j)}(\eta)\}^{g}h^{(j)}(\eta)>0,
 \qquad 0\le g\le5,                                          \tag{6}
\]
each factor in this scalar product having strictly positive entries. In particular,
\[
 p_0^{(0)}=\alpha_{\star}h^{(0)}(\eta)=\frac{5\eta+12}{50}>0. \tag{7}
\]

It remains to check predictive rank. At \((\eta,\zeta)=(0,0)\), direct multiplication of the stopped-series probabilities for the predeclared chart gives
\[
 H=
 \begin{pmatrix}
 1&6/25&2847/25000\\
 509/1000&2847/25000&1506459/25000000\\
 251/1000&3651/50000&601221/25000000
 \end{pmatrix},
 \qquad
 \det H=\frac{257499}{31250000000}\ne0.                      \tag{8}
\]
The two laws have the same stopped series at this boundary, as will also follow from (10) below. Each entry of their respective chart matrices is continuous in \((\eta,\zeta)\). Therefore (8) makes both declared minors nonsingular on a sufficiently small rectangle. A nonsingular three-by-three stopped-Hankel minor gives full-array rank at least three, while a three-state realization gives rank at most three; hence the predictive rank is exactly \(K=3\). Equations (1)--(8), together with the stated sequential construction, prove that both positive-parameter laws belong to \(\mathcal M^{\mathrm{HL}}_{3,5}\).

We next establish observational collision at the boundary \(\zeta=0\). There the first two diagonal entries of every \(B_a^{\star}(0)\) agree, so
\[
 SB_a^{\star}(0)=B_a^{\star}(0)S,
 \qquad
 M_a^{(1)}(\eta,0)=S^{-1}M_a^{(0)}(\eta,0)S,                 \tag{9}
\]
where \(M_a^{(j)}=B_a^{\star}K_0^{(j)}\). Together with \(\alpha^{(1)}=\alpha_{\star}S\), \(h^{(1)}=S^{-1}h^{(0)}\), and \(S\mathbf 1_3=\mathbf 1_3\), multiplication of (9) over any word \(w\) yields
\[
 \alpha^{(1)}M_w^{(1)}\mathbf 1_3
 =\alpha_{\star}M_w^{(0)}\mathbf 1_3,
 \qquad
 \alpha^{(1)}M_w^{(1)}h^{(1)}
 =\alpha_{\star}M_w^{(0)}h^{(0)}.                            \tag{10}
\]
By the definition of the two stopped terminal series, (10) is equality of every risk-terminal and adoption-terminal stopped-word probability. The treated-outcome law is common by construction, so
\[
 P_0^{\eta,0}=P_1^{\eta,0}                                  \tag{11}
\]
for every sufficiently small \(\eta\), although this boundary law need not itself satisfy the hazard-in-emission-algebra restriction when \(\eta>0\).

The support \(\mathcal X\) of a six-date stopped panel with the common deterministic treated path is finite. On the feasible common support, the positive parameter bounds above give a constant \(b>0\) such that the cell probabilities \(p_{\eta,\zeta}(x)\) and \(q_{\eta,\zeta}(x)\) under the two laws are at least \(b\), uniformly on a sufficiently small closed rectangle. Every cell probability is a finite sum of finite products of parameter entries, hence is analytic there. Equation (11), followed by the mean-value theorem in \(\zeta\), therefore gives a finite constant \(C_1\) such that
\[
 \max_{x\in\mathcal X}|p_{\eta,\zeta}(x)-q_{\eta,\zeta}(x)|
 \le C_1\zeta.                                               \tag{12}
\]
Using \(\log u\le u-1\), normalization of both cell vectors, (12), and the lower bound \(b\), we obtain
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \operatorname{KL}(P_0^{\eta,\zeta},P_1^{\eta,\zeta})
 &\le \sum_{x\in\mathcal X}p_{\eta,\zeta}(x)
       \left\{\frac{p_{\eta,\zeta}(x)}{q_{\eta,\zeta}(x)}-1\right\}\\
 &=\sum_{x\in\mathcal X}
   \frac{\{p_{\eta,\zeta}(x)-q_{\eta,\zeta}(x)\}^2}
        {q_{\eta,\zeta}(x)}
 \le \frac{|\mathcal X|C_1^2}{b}\zeta^2.                   \tag{13}
 \end{aligned}
\]
This proves the uniform one-panel divergence bound.

We now calculate the omitted dictionary singular value. For the declared chart, the latent suffix matrix is
\[
 C(\eta,\zeta)
 =\begin{bmatrix}
 \mathbf 1_3&h^{(0)}(\eta)&B_0^{\star}(\zeta)K_0^{(0)}(\eta)h^{(0)}(\eta)
 \end{bmatrix}.                                               \tag{14}
\]
The canonical-realization factorization and the dictionary \((I_3,\bar B_1,\bar B_1^2)\) give
\[
 V_D(\eta,\zeta)
 =C(\eta,\zeta)^{-1}
 \begin{bmatrix}
 \mathbf 1_3&B_1^{\star}(\zeta)\mathbf 1_3&
 \{B_1^{\star}(\zeta)\}^2\mathbf 1_3
 \end{bmatrix}.                                               \tag{15}
\]
The inverse exists near the origin by (8), because the Hankel factorization \(H=RC\) with square factors makes \(C(0,0)\) invertible. Exact rational simplification of (15) at \(\eta=0\) gives
\[
 V_D(0,0)=
 \begin{pmatrix}1&-1/10&-13/50\\0&2&2\\0&0&0\end{pmatrix},
 \qquad
 \det V_D(0,\zeta)
 =-\frac{500\zeta(5\zeta-3)}{51(5\zeta-1)}.                 \tag{16}
\]
At \(\zeta=0\), the first two entries of each vector in the right matrix of (15) agree, and that matrix has rank exactly two. Thus \(\det V_D(\eta,0)=0\) for every small \(\eta\). Since the determinant is continuously differentiable near the origin, the fundamental theorem of calculus gives
\[
 \det V_D(\eta,\zeta)=\zeta d(\eta,\zeta),
 \qquad
 d(\eta,\zeta)=\int_0^1
 \partial_{\zeta}\det V_D(\eta,t\zeta)\,dt.                \tag{17}
\]
The second formula in (16) implies \(d(0,0)=-500/17\). Hence continuity makes \(|d(\eta,\zeta)|\) bounded above and bounded away from zero on a smaller rectangle.

For a rank-two three-by-three matrix, expanding the coefficient of degree one in the characteristic polynomial of its Gram matrix shows directly that the product of the two nonzero squared singular values equals the sum of the squares of all two-by-two minors. Applying this elementary identity to the first matrix in (16) gives
\[
 \sigma_1\{V_D(0,0)\}\sigma_2\{V_D(0,0)\}
 =\frac{2\sqrt{1266}}{25}.                                   \tag{18}
\]
Singular values are continuous in the matrix entries. Combining (17)--(18) with
\[
 \sigma_1(V_D)\sigma_2(V_D)\sigma_3(V_D)=|\det V_D|          \tag{19}
\]
therefore yields, uniformly up to fixed multiplicative constants,
\[
 \sigma_3\{V_D(\eta,\zeta)\}=\Theta(\zeta),
 \qquad
 \frac{\sigma_3\{V_D(\eta,\zeta)\}}{\zeta}
 \longrightarrow
 \frac{500/17}{2\sqrt{1266}/25}
 =\frac{6250}{17\sqrt{1266}}                                 \tag{20}
\]
as \((\eta,\zeta)\to(0,0)\) through positive values.

We next derive the causal separation. Because \(g=0\), \(r=1\), and \(\nu(1)=1\), \(\nu(0)=0\), the untreated cohort means in the two legal latent coordinates are
\[
 (\mu^0_{0,1})^{(j)}
 =\frac{\alpha^{(j)}\operatorname{diag}\{h^{(j)}(\eta)\}
 P^{(j)}(\eta)B_1^{\star}(\zeta)\mathbf 1_3}
 {\alpha^{(j)}h^{(j)}(\eta)},
 \qquad j=0,1.                                                \tag{21}
\]
The denominators are positive by (6). Substituting the rational matrices from the construction into (21), putting the two fractions over their common denominator, and collecting monomials gives
\[
 \Delta(\eta,\zeta)
 =-\frac{3\{87500\eta^3\zeta+18000\eta^2\zeta+9000\eta^2+22015\eta\zeta+53550\eta-3468\zeta\}}
 {400(5\eta+12)(25\eta-17)(25\eta+17)}.                    \tag{22}
\]
The denominator is nonzero near the origin. Taylor expansion of this rational function at the origin, with \(\eta\zeta=O(\zeta)\) on a bounded rectangle, gives
\[
 \Delta(\eta,\zeta)=\frac{63}{544}\eta+O(\eta^2+\zeta).   \tag{23}
\]
At the collision boundary and any sufficiently small fixed \(\eta_0>0\), the exact value
\[
 \Delta(\eta_0,0)
 =-\frac{3(9000\eta_0^2+53550\eta_0)}
 {400(5\eta_0+12)(625\eta_0^2-289)}>0                       \tag{24}
\]
is nonzero. Since the treated outcome is the same deterministic constant under the two laws, the difference of their ATT values is \(-\Delta(\eta,\zeta)\); in particular, its absolute magnitude is \(|\Delta(\eta,\zeta)|\).

Let now \(a_N,b_N>0\) satisfy \(Nb_N^2\to0\) and \(b_N=o(a_N)\). Define the one-panel chi-square quantity in the direction used in (13) by
\[
 \chi_N^2=\sum_{x\in\mathcal X}
 \frac{\{p_{a_N,b_N}(x)-q_{a_N,b_N}(x)\}^2}
 {q_{a_N,b_N}(x)}=O(b_N^2).                                  \tag{25}
\]
Factoring the finite product sum proves directly that
\[
 1+\chi^2\!\left((P_0^{a_N,b_N})^{\otimes N},
                  (P_1^{a_N,b_N})^{\otimes N}\right)
 =(1+\chi_N^2)^N.                                             \tag{26}
\]
The right side minus one is at most \(\exp(N\chi_N^2)-1=o(1)\). Cauchy--Schwarz then gives
\[
 \left\|(P_0^{a_N,b_N})^{\otimes N}
       -(P_1^{a_N,b_N})^{\otimes N}\right\|_{\mathrm{TV}}
 \le\frac12\sqrt{\chi^2\!\left((P_0^{a_N,b_N})^{\otimes N},
                  (P_1^{a_N,b_N})^{\otimes N}\right)}
 \longrightarrow0.                                           \tag{27}
\]
If \(a_N\to0\), (23) and \(b_N=o(a_N)\) give
\[
 |\tau_{0,1}(P_1^{a_N,b_N})-
   \tau_{0,1}(P_0^{a_N,b_N})|
 =\left(\frac{63}{544}+o(1)\right)a_N.                      \tag{28}
\]
If \(a_N\equiv\eta_0>0\), continuity of (22) and (24) instead gives convergence of the absolute ATT gap to \(\Delta(\eta_0,0)>0\). Moreover, (20) and \(Nb_N^2\to0\) imply
\[
 \frac{\sigma_3(V_D)}{\rho_N}
 =O\!\left(\frac{b_N\sqrt N}{\sqrt{\log N}}\right)
 =o(1).                                                       \tag{29}
\]
For every \(N\), positivity of \(b_N\) and (17)--(20) gives \(\sigma_3(V_D)>0\). Thus eventually \(0<\sigma_3(V_D)\le\rho_N\), which is precisely the sampling-noise component of the declared gray zone.

We finally prove the two statistical impossibilities using the fixed-\(\eta_0\) sequence, for example with \(b_N=N^{-1}\). Let \(\vartheta_{j,N}=\tau_{0,1}(P_j^{\eta_0,b_N})\) and let \(\delta=\Delta(\eta_0,0)>0\). By (24), \(|\vartheta_{1,N}-\vartheta_{0,N}|\to\delta\), while (27) gives merging product laws. If an estimator \(\widehat\vartheta_N\) were uniformly consistent over any class containing these laws, then for all large \(N\) the events
\[
 A_{j,N}=\{|\widehat\vartheta_N-\vartheta_{j,N}|<\delta/3\},
 \qquad j=0,1,                                                 \tag{30}
\]
would have probability tending to one under their respective product laws. Total-variation merging transfers the probability of \(A_{1,N}\) to the zeroth product law. But \(A_{0,N}\cap A_{1,N}=\varnothing\) for large \(N\), contradicting that both then have probability tending to one under the zeroth law. Uniform consistency is therefore impossible.

Similarly, let \(C_N\) be a random confidence set with coverage at least \(1-\alpha_0-o(1)\) under both product laws, where \(\alpha_0<1/2\). Total-variation merging and the union bound imply under the zeroth product law that
\[
 \Pr\{\vartheta_{0,N}\in C_N,\ \vartheta_{1,N}\in C_N\}
 \ge1-2\alpha_0-o(1)>0.                                      \tag{31}
\]
On the event in (31), \(\operatorname{diam}(C_N)\ge|\vartheta_{1,N}-\vartheta_{0,N}|\to\delta\). Hence uniformly honest diameter \(o(1)\) in probability is impossible.

For the declared specialization \(\eta_N=N^{-1/4}\), \(\zeta_N=N^{-1}\), the sequence premises hold because \(N\zeta_N^2=N^{-1}\to0\) and \(\zeta_N/\eta_N=N^{-3/4}\to0\). Equations (20), (27)--(29) become
\[
 \sigma_3(V_D)=\left(\frac{6250}{17\sqrt{1266}}+o(1)\right)N^{-1},
 \quad
 \|(P_{W,N}^{(0)})^{\otimes N}-(P_{W,N}^{(1)})^{\otimes N}\|_{\mathrm{TV}}\to0,
 \quad
 |\vartheta_{1,N}-\vartheta_{0,N}|=\left(\frac{63}{544}+o(1)\right)N^{-1/4}. \tag{32}
\]
Repeating (31) with the last separation in (32) rules out uniformly honest diameter \(o(N^{-1/4})\) over that pair. This proves every assertion.

proposed.statement: Fix \(K=3\), \(T=5\), and the cohort--lag pair \((g,r)=(0,1)\). Along \(\mathfrak C_N\), both six-date realizations have strictly positive initial probabilities, transitions, emissions, interior hazards, and \(p_0>0\) for all sufficiently large \(N\). Their stopped-word probabilities agree exactly when \(\zeta_N=0\); at the declared \(\zeta_N=N^{-1}\), \(\operatorname{KL}(P_{W,N}^{(0)},P_{W,N}^{(1)})=O(\zeta_N^2)\) and \(\operatorname{KL}((P_{W,N}^{(0)})^{\otimes N},(P_{W,N}^{(1)})^{\otimes N})=O(N\zeta_N^2)=O(N^{-1})\). Under \(P_{W,N}^{(0)}\), the declared canonical matrix with \(d=2\) satisfies \(\sigma_3(V_D)=(10.33271+o(1))\zeta_N\), while \((\mu^0_{0,1})^{(1)}-(\mu^0_{0,1})^{(0)}=63\eta_N/544+o(\eta_N)\); the common deterministic treated outcome gives the opposite gap for \(\tau_{0,1}\). Hence the product-law total variation tends to zero, the \(\tau_{0,1}\) separation is of order \(N^{-1/4}\), this path lies in \(0<\sigma_3(V_D)\le\rho_N\), and for every fixed \(\alpha_0<1/2\) no confidence band for \(\tau_{0,1}\) can have uniform \(1-\alpha_0\) coverage over this pair and diameter \(o(N^{-1/4})\) in probability under both product laws.
